journeys.today: Tourist longboats (~$80-150 charter, 1.5 hr each way) cause wake and disturbance in the mangrove channels — exactly what the conservation objective wants minimized.
journeys.with_navier: Silent zero-wake foiling tour boat — 35 min each way; the platform IS the eco-credential and unlocks premium pricing the operators currently can't access.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II (or a short-hop derivative) is the natural fit for both the dense ~1 nm penambang corridor and the 8-11 nm cultural/eco-tour overlays. Silent zero-wake is the conservation use case AND the premium-pricing advantage — operationally, mangrove and water-village access need exactly what foiling-electric delivers.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR extends to cross-Brunei-Bay corridors (Muara ↔ Labuan ~25 nm, Muara ↔ Lawas ~40 nm) and opens a regional Sabah/Sarawak adjacent footprint without local charging infrastructure — relevant if a Borneo cross-border lane develops.

regulatory_note: Brunei Maritime and Port Authority (BMPA) governs all commercial water transit. Sharia law context: alcohol prohibition in public — design service tier accordingly (alcohol-free is a feature for the family/Islamic-tourism segment). Patronage matters: Sultan-endorsed initiatives clear approval pathways; Brunei Tourism Board is the natural government channel. NO outreach to Bruneian royal household or sovereign channels without coordinated intro — flag as `hold_authority: pending_intro` until partnership pathway confirmed.
seasonality: Year-round tropical (26-32°C); November-February wetter monsoon but bay-protected water; visitor peak Aug-Oct (Brunei Maritime Festival, Sultan's Birthday). Daily resident commute is constant 365 days/year — the rare brief with zero seasonality on the base-load segment.

summary: Kampong Ayer is a UNESCO-recognized cluster of 42 stilt villages housing ~30,000 residents in the heart of the capital. Daily life runs on ~300 water taxis (penambangs) — small wooden boats with 25-40 hp outboards making constant cross-river hops between Kampong Ayer and the city proper, ferrying residents to schools, government offices, and the central market. Tourism overlays this base demand with cultural-village tours, mosque visits (Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien, Jame'Asr Hassanil Bolkiah), and proboscis-monkey mangrove cruises into Brunei Bay. Brunei's 2025-2035 Tourism Master Plan explicitly targets eco-luxury repositioning, and the conservative sharia context creates a natural alcohol-free, family-segment opportunity for premium silent transit.
tagline: The world's largest water village — 30,000 residents on stilts over the Brunei River — has run on water taxis for 200+ years. Electrification of the penambang fleet is the most natural decarbonization story in Southeast Asia.

use_cases.body: Replace highest-polluting 2-stroke water taxis serving daily Kampong Ayer commute with electric short-hop fleet. Demand is base-load (residents go to work every day), so utilization is high.
